title: Sanjeev Verma v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Laxmi Kanta Mohapatra and Rakesh Srivastava, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed; Clause 4.4 application to be considered within 15 days.
headnote: An occupier whose owner has had supply disconnected and refuses consent for a new connection may apply for an independent connection under Clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed with a direction that a fresh Clause 4.4 application, if made, be considered and decided within 15 days.
facts: The petitioner claimed to be in possession of a house belonging to respondent no. 5. Electricity to the premises was disconnected on the owner's instructions, and the owner refused to let the petitioner take a new connection. The petitioner had already represented to the distribution licensee seeking supply. He then filed this writ petition seeking electricity despite the owner's refusal.

holding_units.topic: independent connection by occupier without owner consent
holding_units.holding: A lessee, tenant or occupier who cannot obtain the owner's consent may apply for an independent electricity connection under Clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the petitioner files a fresh application under that clause, the licensee shall consider it and decide within 15 days of submission.

not_decided.point: Merits of the petitioner's entitlement to a new connection, and validity of the disconnection at the owner's instance
not_decided.note: The Court only pointed the petitioner to Clause 4.4 and directed consideration of a fresh application.
